extracted.intended_audience: serious readers, literary critics, and aspiring novelists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reading, judging, and understanding how novels are made; explains the reader's and critic's role in reconstructing a book's form and analyzes narrative methods and techniques for producing effective fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book has a form (form, design, composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel is a thing to which a shape is ascribable—its form, design, and composition are real properties that make the book what it is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the novel’s shape is good or bad and whether it matters; check proportion, design and whether the form expresses the subject. Note difficulty: memory and the novel’s temporal flow make the form hard to perceive, so deliberate reconstruction is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read aright / creative reading
rubrics_metrics.description: The beginning of criticism is to read aright: deliberately watch the book itself rather than merely losing oneself in its scenes and characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice 'creative reading' (Emerson’s phrase): hold the novel at a distance, re-create it page by page as a unified work, and deliberately shape the impressions into a stable image of the book. This takes effort and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader as co-creator / critic-as-novelist
rubrics_metrics.description: The critical reader must act as a novelist in part — recreating, selecting and arranging the material given by the author to form the book in his own mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume the author's work will be transferred intact into the reader's mind; the critic shares responsibility for the book’s realized form and must handle the 'stuff' of impressions workmanlike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and arrangement (authorial selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelist’s primary craft is selection and arrangement: lifting, rejecting, re-making life into situations that can be ordered in a single design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a book, examine whether the author's selection and arrangement suit the subject: did the author start from the heart of the subject, or diverge? Diagnose where the treatment has gone wrong if the form fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and use different narrative 'substances' or forms
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel is made of various forms of narrative (dramatic, pictorial, scenic, generalized, etc.)—these are the substances from which a book is built.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which narrative modes appear, perceive their demands and qualities, and judge how the author uses or mixes them. The critic must learn these forms by close, conscious reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and appropriate function of picture vs drama
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between pictorial (broad survey, accumulation of impressions) and dramatic (active scene-based) narrative methods; each has its proper function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the novelist holds picture and drama to their natural functions: picture suits long reaches over time/space and piling impressions; drama delivers the final structural strokes in scenes that advance the story. Misuse or confusion of the two can weaken form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic scene effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: A dramatic scene should be active—every part engaged and advancing the story—yet feel effortless and proper to its task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for scenes that 'mark and affirm the structural lines' of the story (example: Madame Bovary). Scenes must not attempt tasks inappropriate to them or feel forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial method strengths and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictorial reporting gives accumulated impressions across time/space but risks thinness and flatness if treated as direct life rather than as mediated art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge pictorial passages by their ability to accumulate impression without losing coherence; recognize thinness but also the opportunity to dramatize the narrator's mind (the 'mirror') to convert apparent weakness into strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of consciousness / mediated narration ('mind as mirror')
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling a story through a constituted consciousness (interposing a mind between author and reader) can dramatize and strengthen material that would be mere pictorial report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the novelist uses a focal consciousness to transform pictorial description into dramatic material; this technique can give direct view of the narrator’s mind and thereby produce stronger effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of detail and character in large canvases
rubrics_metrics.description: Even in panoramic, populous novels the author must maintain control over characters and scenes so that parts are lucid and intentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the author loses grip amid profusion: check for faltering hold on characters, hesitating intention in scenes, and whether parts maintain clarity even if the whole is vast (Tolstoy example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy vs prodigality of material
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel may be profuse (like a 'world') or economical; either can succeed, but excess material can obscure form unless skillfully handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether profusion serves an intention or merely distracts; sometimes a profuse world suffices by sheer life, but composition should still provide coherence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory-resilience of pages (durability of writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages that are well fashioned resist the treachery of memory and remain with the reader; the craft should aim at durable, memorable passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the novelist's success in producing scenes, descriptions and characters that survive imperfect memory—detailed, well-made pages are likelier to endure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical study: analyse methods used to create effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism should concentrate on how novels are made: follow the methods of successful novelists to see exactly how scenes and figures are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read constructively and questioningly; determine the specific arts and devices by which episodes are given relief and characters made vivid; build a technical vocabulary for effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming and diagnosing faults in form
rubrics_metrics.description: If a book’s form is imperfect, the critic should identify whether the fault lies in treatment, divergence from the subject, or the subject’s poverty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace where the development breaks or contradicts the subject; ask whether a better proceeding could have been conceived and named; follow the author's course back to its choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcome shyness about analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics should not be inhibited by the feeling that analysis destroys the novel’s illusion; dissection is legitimate and necessary for understanding craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that explaining how a novel works does not necessarily spoil it; the pleasure of creation and the critic’s task of remaking the book justify analytical inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept imprecision of critical language but seek usable terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Language for criticizing fiction is metaphorical and imprecise (colors, values, perspective), but critics should still try to develop and use technical terms for narrative effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the limits of metaphors yet attempt to round out a critical vocabulary by careful study of recurring methods and effects; do not be deterred by lack of exact nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle sequence and temporal architecture (procession → welded mass)
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel is both a procession of time-bound impressions and should be apprehended as a welded mass (a single form) after reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically marshal the story’s sequence into a coherent structure; aim to see how successive fragments combine into the book’s overall architecture and whether that architecture succeeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and evaluate mixtures and modifications of narrative modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelists often mix narrative modes; critics should detect these mixtures and assess whether combinations are effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note where modes overlap (e.g., scenic + pictorial + dramatic), how the mixes function, and whether their commingling produces coherent effects or muddles form.
